title: Your game version is different from the server's
explanation: The server runs a different Minecraft version than you do.
fix: Check the server's version (server list or website) and launch that exact version. Some servers also need a specific mod loader.

title: The server is older than your game
explanation: You are on a newer Minecraft version than the server supports.
fix: Launch the older version the server uses, or ask the owner when they plan to update.

title: You're not on the whitelist
explanation: This server only lets approved players join.
fix: Ask the server owner or staff to add your exact username. Make sure you are logged in with the right account.

title: You are banned from this server
explanation: A staff member banned your account or your IP address.
fix: Read the ban message for a reason or appeal link. If it is an IP ban, anyone sharing your network may be affected too.

title: The server is full
explanation: All player slots are taken right now.
fix: Try again in a few minutes. Some servers have a priority or rank slot for supporters.

title: Minecraft couldn't verify your account
explanation: Your login session expired, or Mojang/Microsoft's login servers are having trouble.
fix: Fully close and reopen the launcher, then sign in again. If it keeps happening, check whether Minecraft's login services are down.

title: Your account is already connected
explanation: The same account joined from another place, or your old connection hasn't timed out yet.
fix: Close any other Minecraft window or device using this account, wait about 30 seconds, then rejoin.

title: The server requires its resource pack
explanation: You declined or failed to download the pack this server requires.
fix: In the server list, edit the server and set Server Resource Packs to Enabled (or Prompt and accept it). If the download fails, check your internet.

title: Mods don't match the server
explanation: The server and your game have different mods or mod versions, or one side is modded and the other isn't.
fix: Install exactly the modpack/mod versions the server lists. If the server is vanilla or a plugin server, remove mods that change gameplay.

title: Chat signing or profile problem
explanation: The server requires a secure, verified chat profile, or your profile key is out of sync.
fix: Restart the launcher and sign in again. Also check that your Microsoft account has multiplayer and chat enabled in its privacy settings.

title: Kicked for looking like you were flying
explanation: The server's anti-cheat thought you were flying, often caused by lag or a mod.
fix: Disable mods that change movement and avoid long falls while lagging. Tell staff if you were not cheating.

title: Kicked for spamming
explanation: You sent chat messages or commands too quickly.
fix: Wait a moment and rejoin, then slow down. Macros and keybinds that send commands can trigger this.

title: Kicked for being idle
explanation: You didn't move for longer than the server allows.
fix: Rejoin. Standing still on an AFK-kick server will get you kicked again.

title: That server address doesn't exist
explanation: Minecraft couldn't find a server at that address, or you have no internet.
fix: Check the address for typos and extra spaces. Make sure you are online and try a different website to confirm.

title: The server refused the connection
explanation: Nothing is accepting connections at that address and port. The server is usually offline, restarting, or the port is wrong.
fix: Wait a minute and try again. Double-check the address and port, and ask the owner if the server is online.

title: The connection timed out
explanation: The server didn't answer in time. Common causes are a laggy connection, a very busy server, or a firewall blocking the connection.
fix: Try again, switch from Wi-Fi to a wired or different network, and turn off VPNs. If you're hosting, check port forwarding and the firewall.

title: The server shut down or restarted
explanation: The server was stopped, restarted, or crashed while you were connected.
fix: Wait a few minutes and rejoin. Check the server's Discord or status page.

title: The connection was cut off
explanation: The connection dropped suddenly. This is usually your network, a server crash, or a firewall or antivirus closing the connection.
fix: Rejoin and check your internet. If it happens repeatedly, try another network and pause VPNs or overly strict security software.

title: Your game and the server couldn't understand each other
explanation: A network packet was broken or unexpected. Common causes are a version mismatch, a mod interfering with networking, or a misconfigured proxy on the server.
fix: Make sure your version matches the server's and try without mods. If it still happens on a vanilla client, tell the server owner.

title: The connection to the server was lost
explanation: Minecraft doesn't have a more specific reason for this one.
fix: Rejoin, and check your internet. If the line above gives more detail, use that to search or to ask the server owner.
